title: Fair prices or market prices?
hook: Charge each buyer the harm it does to others. Is that what a market would charge?

knows: raising prices on over-demanded items until each buyer gets a preferred item clears a matching market (prices-sort-the-buyers)
the VCG rule: pay the harm you cause others (pay-for-the-harm-you-do)
doesNotKnow: that charging each buyer the harm they cause gives exactly the market-clearing prices found by raising prices

misconception: Prices from a fairness rule (pay the harm) and prices from supply and demand are unrelated.
objective: The learner can compute each buyer's harm (the others' best total without it minus what they get with it) in a 3 × 3 matching market and see that the harms equal the market-clearing prices of the items those buyers get.

claims.text: In the stage's table the best assignment is x–a, y–c, z–b, with total value 23.
claims.source: Demo.tsx best(): enumeration of all 6 assignments; the optimum is unique. Valuations from the brief (company/domains/briefs/economics.markets.md #23).

claims.text: x's presence costs the others 14 − 11 = 3, z's costs 19 − 18 = 1, and y's costs 17 − 17 = 0, so harm payments total $4.
claims.source: Demo.tsx WITHOUT, WITH, HARM. Without x: y–b 7 + z–a 7 = 14, with x: y 6 + z 5 = 11. Without z: x–a 12 + y–b 7 = 19, with z: 12 + 6 = 18. Without y: x–a 12 + z–b 5 = 17, with y: 12 + 5 = 17. Re-run in node by the builder.

claims.text: Raising prices clears this market at a $3, b $1, c $0 (total $4), and each buyer's harm equals the price of the item it gets.
claims.source: Demo.tsx clearingPrices(): ascending procedure (raise a constricted set's preferred items by 1, renormalise to a minimum of 0) ends at 3, 1, 0 whichever constricted set is chosen first (builder checked smallest and largest). Builder brute force over integer prices 0 to 12: 79 clearing price vectors, the unique smallest-total one is 3, 1, 0. Harms: x (gets a) 3, z (gets b) 1, y (gets c) 0.

claims.text: In matching markets like this, harm (VCG) prices always clear the market, and are the lowest prices that do.
claims.source: Theorem: Leonard (1983), 'Elicitation of honest preferences for the assignment of individuals to positions', Journal of Political Economy 91(3); Easley and Kleinberg (2010) ch. 15 (advanced section); Kern, Manthey and Uetz, arXiv 1604.04157. Fact-checker confirms the exact statement.

recall.question: In a matching market, removing buyer Q would let the others gain $5 in total. Q gets item k in the best assignment. What is k's lowest market-clearing price?
options: It cannot be told without the full supply and demand
recall.why: Q's harm to the others is $5, and in such markets the harm a buyer causes is the lowest clearing price of the item it gets.
